title: JDK vs JRE vs JVM
question: What is the difference between JDK, JRE and JVM?
answer: JVM executes Java bytecode. JRE provides the JVM plus runtime libraries. JDK provides the JRE/runtime plus development tools such as javac.
example: javac Hello.java -> Hello.class -> JVM executes bytecode
notes: Remember: JDK = develop, JRE = run, JVM = execute.

title: HashMap Internal Working
question: How does HashMap work internally?
answer: HashMap uses an array of buckets. A key's hash is processed to determine a bucket. Collisions are stored in nodes and may be treeified under certain conditions in Java 8+.
notes: Remember: hash -> bucket -> node -> collision -> list/tree.
